title.narrative: UNFPA: Addressing the needs of women and girls in the regional Syria crisis
UNFPA: Att ta itu med kvinnors och flickors behov i den regionala Syrien-krisen

description.narrative:
Den föreslagna programplaneringen omfattar perioden från 1 januari 2021 till 31 december 2023 och är en fortsättning på samma program som tidigare har finansierats för Syrien, Jordanien, Libanon, Turkiet och Turkiet gränsöverskridande av the United Nations Population Fund(UNFPA). Den totala budgeten för programmet omfattar 180 000 000 SEK (20031,15 MUSD) och har fyra huvudmålsättningar:
- Öka tillgängligheten och tillgången till specialiserade och integrerade SRH- och GBV-tjänster, särskilt för kvinnor, flickor och personer med funktionsnedsättning.
- Förbättra kapaciteten för de tjänster som levereras och hos samarbetsspartners för att tillhandahålla högkvalitativa, inkluderande och omfattande GBV- och RH-tjänster.
- Utmana de negativa sociala normerna som förhindrar stärkandet av kvinnors och flickors rättigheter.
- Öka dialogen med regeringar, grupper, samhällen och andra intressenter för att förbättra skyddet för och hälsan hos kvinnor, flickor, ungdomar och andra utsatta grupper.

In the proposed programming from 01 January 2021 till 31 December 2023 is a continuation of the same programe that has been funded previously covering Syria, Jordan, Lebanon, Turkey and Turkey cross border implemented by the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA). The budget is 180 000 000 SEK 820,031,15 MUSD) and has four main objectives:
- Increase the availability of and access to specialized and integrated SRH and GBV services, especially for women, girls, and persons with disabilities.
- Improve capacity of service and implementing partners to provide high-quality, inclusive, and comprehensive GBV and RH services.
- Challenge the negative social norms that prevent the empowerment of women and girls.
- Increase advocacy efforts with governments, advocacy groups, communities, and other stakeholders to improve the protection and health of women, girls, adolescents, and other vulnerable groups.

The proposed UNFPA Programme:Addressing the needs of women and girls in the regional Syria crisis seeks to achieve an overall goal to increase the sense of well being of women and girls accessing UNFPA programmes and supported services (including WGSS, Youth programmes, Health facilities) and activities. The specific objectives are: 1) Increase the availability of and access to specialised and integrated SRH and GBV services, especially for women, girls, and persons with disabilities. 2) Improve capacity of service and implementing partners to provide high-quality, inclusive, and comprehensive GBV and RH services. 3) Challenge the negative social norms that prevent the empowerment of women and girls. 4) Increase advocacy efforts with governments, advocacy groups, communities, and other stakeholders to improve the protection and health of women, girls, adolescents, and other vulnerable groups.

description.narrative:
Results from 2023
Results in relation to increased access to specialised integrated SRH and GBV services:
In government-controlled Syria (GoS), UNFPA has during 2023 continued to support essential SRH services to the most vulnerable people across 14 governorates through 184 primary health facilities and mobile teams, of which Sweden covered the staffing and operational costs of 14 service delivery points, reaching 54 154 beneficiaries with SRH services. With the funding from Sweden, UNFPA and their partners reached 55 193 beneficiaries with GBV services, provided through 7 Women and Girls Safe Spaces in Aleppo, Deir-Ez-Zor, Homs, Rural Damascus and Damascus. The supported WGSSs played a critical role within the local communities as they enables women and girls' access to GBV prevention and response services, including GBV case management, psyco-social support and awareness raising. Some of the WGSS have established mobile teams to reach women and girls with limited access.
In North-West Syria, the Gaziantep Cross-Boarder UNFPA office has reached 176 710 beneficiaries with SRH services (272 by Swedish funded operations), through 11 primary health facilities and mobile teams, all of which were able to provide EmOC. During 2023, UNFPA continued to increase the capacity of its partners to ensure that services are accessable to all groups, including persons with disabilities and older women. In partnership with WHO, staff has increased their capacity to adress social inclusion issues. Through Swedish funding, 11 533 beneficiaries were receiving GBV services from 5 WGSS in the governorates Aleppo and Idlib. During the reporting year, UNFPA has commited to ensure life skills sessions offered at the WGSSs are more gender-transformative, based on recomendations from third party monitoring.
During 2023, UNFPA Jordan has focused on the expansion of service provision, enhancement of infrastructure, and the implementation of innovative solutions to reach vulnerable populations. In Jordan, Swedish support has enabled UNFPA to enhance support to six static clinics, offering expanded SRH services in host communities and reaching 20 532 beneficiaries with a particular focus on marginalised women and girls in areas such as Karak, Madaba and Amman. To improve access to essential pharmaceuticals for SRH services, JCO has implemented a medication voucher program during 2023, issuing targeted vouchers enabling 1 150 women and girls to obtain necessary SRH medications. The success of the program was recognized with the prestigious 2023 Innovation Award, highlighting its effectiveness. UNFPA Jordans commitment to refine the cash and voucher assistance program underscores its dedication to ensuring access to sexual and reproductive health rights, even in the most challenging circumstances.
Swedish funds have enhanced GBV service delivery through six WGSSs in Madaba, Sweileh, Karak, Zarqa and two sites in Amman, providing GBV prevention and response services to 16 146 individuals, including virtual case management services, referrals, psychosocial support, awareness-raising, counselling and outreach services via phone or WhatsApp. Moreover, outreach interventions and awareness-raising sessions on GBV benefited 9 133 beneficiaries and the Swedish funding contributed to reaching 35 165 women and girls with empowerment and recreational activities. UNFPA Jordan reports that the integration of GBV services with SRH care, along with the provision of virtual case management and outreach services, has significantly enhanced the accessibility and comprehensiveness of support to GBV survivors.
UNFPA Jordan continued the integration of cash assistance within the GBV case management which according to their analysis of the post distribution monitoring, significantly contributes to beneficiaries safety and well-being with a notable positive impact on immediate GBV risk mitigation and accessibility to urgent GBV services.
In Lebanon the Swedish funding has contributed to maintaining the availability of and access to specialised and integrated SRH and GBV services through three health facilities and one medical mobile unit, providing 4 625 beneficiaries with SRH services. Comprehensive and specialized GBV services were provided in four static WGSSs and nine mobile, reaching 9 731 beneficiaries, a number well above the target. The Lebanon office reports a rise in GBV as a consequence of the economic crisis, with forced marriage and sexual violence as the third and fourth most reported types of violence, and that displaced Syrians constitute the majority of the population experiencing GBV incidents. The higher than target beneficiaries reached, reflects an increase in demand for GBV services. However, the escalation in fuel prices and communication costs makes it more difficult for survivors of violence to access services provided, why the Lebanon office has continued to offer cash for transportation and supported the establishment of more mobile clinics and safe spaces to reach the more marginalized groups. As an additional effort to reach marginalized people, two of the Implementing partners supported, specializes in making their services available for LGBTQI persons and people with disabilities. Specially the LGBTQI communities are marginally targeted in the overall regional response.
The Türkiye Country Office has continuously responded to the earthquake throughout 2023, while continuing to provide GBV and SRH interventions for refugees and host communities also in regions that were not affected by the earthquake. The funds from Sweden have financed the operations of 3 Women and Girls Safe Spaces (WGSS) throughout the year, of which 2 are located in the earthquake affected region, and SRH and GBV interventions in earthquake affected Kahramanmaras and Gaziantep. Through the WGSS and interventions in Kahramanmaras and Gazientep, 23 547 beneficiaries were reached with SRH services and 18 465 with GBV prevention and response services during the year, thanks to Swedens support. The reached beneficiaries are above the target, which UNFPA reflects is due to the targeted interventions in the earthquake affected areas. Efforts have been made to make the services provided more accessible for people with disabilities (PWD) through trainings on disability inclusion to all UNFPA SRH service providers in Türkiye.
Results in terms of improved capacity of service and implementing partners to provide high quality, inclusive, and comprehensive GBV and RH services:
In GoS, UNFPA has provided capacity building initiatives for 573 health professional staff with Swedish funding, on topics including breast cancer early detection, clinical management of rape, high-risk pregnancy care, integration of SRH with adolescent health services, intrauterine device insertion techniques among others. In order to increase the quality of care and better respond to the needs of GBV survivors, UNFPA Syria provided training for 276 GBV service providers on basic counselling, psychosocial support and referral indicators, as well on gender mainstreaming and gender analysis and GBV basics specially for IPs in Latakia. The target for people trained on RH-topics for 2023 were set to 900 for the Syria Office, but it is not commented on why a much lower number of people were reached.
In NWS, UNFPA and their IPs conducted training sessions for 122 service providers covering topics such as GBV referral pathways, integrating older women in GBV programming, protection from sexual exploitation and abuse among other. Post-training assessments revealed that all participants who underwent testing showed improvement from their pretest scores.
UNFPA Jordan has focused on enhancing skills, knowledge, and infrastructure to ensure the delivery of superior GBV and SRH services. One key strategy has been the implemented training programs for healthcare providers in host communities covering topics such as antenatal care, early delivery complications, postpartum and newborn care, and the neonatal resuscitation program. Capacity building within the existing healthcare system was another critical aspect of Jordans approach. That involved the provision of necessary resources and support to enhance the quality of SRH services. And thirdly, UNFPA Jordan supported initiatives aimed at enhancing the integration of GBV services with SRH care, providing comprehensive support for survivors. Initiatives like the integration of cash assistance within GBV case management illustrated the commitment to innovative solutions that address the multifaceted needs of GBV survivors. A total of 67 people were trained on different topics. Through partnerships with the Jordanian MoH, UNFPA Jordan has worked to integrate SRH services into national healthcare systems, further enhancing the capacity of the system to deliver high-quality care, with an emphasis on expanding services to vulnerable communities, including Syrian refugees.
To improve the capacity and quality of services provided, UNFPA Lebanon conducted an assessment of Swedish supported IPs and analysed the relevance, effectiveness, and quality of services and support provided in their WGSSs. The exercise included validation from beneficiaries, contributing to increased ownership and empowerment of the women and girls participating. Furthermore, a workshop on the legal aspects of GBV was held with the aim to better improve access of women and girls survivors to legal assistance services and information. A total of 100 people were trained during 2023.
In Türkiye, the capacity of service and implementing partners to provide high quality, inclusive, and comprehensive GBV and RH services, has been improved by capacity building interventions focusing for example on GBV in emergencies, reaching 67 people, among them psychologists and social service experts at WGSS. The number of people trained is above the target, which was zero for 2023, but low in comparison to previous years. Regardless of people trained a specific year, the percentage of sampled individuals supported with GBV or SRH services, stating that they are satisfied with the quality of the support provided has been quite consistent during the programme period. The capacities and resilience of GBV service providers have also been maintained through regular psychosocial support supervision and self-care-sessions throughout the year.
Results in terms of challenging the negative social norms that prevent the empowerment of women and girls:
UNFPA Syria has continued the work on the Indashakirwa GBV primary prevention model with the pilot in Aleppo, consisting of integrated and targeted programming addressing harmful masculinities and womens and girls agency and autonomy. Less than half the number of target beneficiaries (180 compared to the target of 400) were reached during 2023, a result of the earthquake after which many enrolled couples withdrew from the programme activities due to their financial situation and displacement.
In NWS the Adolescent Mothers against All Odds (AMAL) Initiative is implemented through five WGSS, reaching 430 participants during 2023 with Swedish funds. The AMAL model aims to promote healthy timing and spacing of pregnancies, increase awareness to change unequal gender and social norms, and enhance collective self-efficiency to adopt and maintain positive social change, with strong positive effect on participating young mothers self-esteem and confidence. In Lebanon, the AMAL initiative was implemented in Akkar and Tripoli with 251 adolecent girls. Swedish funds have also enabled UNFPA Lebanon to contextualise the Social, Economic, and Health Assets Building Framework, and promote awareness of the Sexual Harassment Law 205 specially targeting public and private sector employers through an online tool developed during the year.
The Jordan office explains the comprehensive approach with targeted initiatives aimed at transforming societal attitudes and behaviours including collaborations with the Ministry of Education on comprehensive sexuality education, engagement in community-led initiatives addressing discriminatory gender and social norms, a study of the economic cost of violence providing empirical evidence, and the continued support to the National taskforce on child marriage.
Swedish funds have not funded any specific activities in Türkiye challenging negative social norms.
Results in terms of Increased advocacy efforts with governments, advocacy groups, communities, and other stakeholders to improve the protection and health of women, girls, adolescents, and other vulnerable groups:
During the 16 Days of Activism against GBV, UNFPA Syria implemented a number of activities including raising awareness on the root causes of GBV in Syrian society and the role of parental education in identifying negative gender stereotypes.
The Jordan Office reports a number of initiatives contributing to the objective, such as capacity building sessions for service providers and advocacy groups focusing on GBV safe referrals and case management, awareness campaigns marking several international days targeting the public awareness, research and studies, support for National Plans and Taskforces, and engagement in international frameworks and celebrations. The support to the National Taskforce on Child Marriage and the Youth, Peace and Security agenda has aimed to ensure that national plans reflect a comprehensive approach to protecting and improving the health of women, girls, adolescents, and other vulnerable groups.
During 2023, the Lebanon Office presented the results of two studies funded by the Swedish support, one on Intimate Partner Violence and one on Obstetric Violence in relation to the World Health Day, to leverage the opportunities to spur evidence-based policy dialogue.
The Cross-Border Office and the Türkiye Office does not report any results in relation to this objective.
